sources.title: Handley Page Halifax LW693 (WMR-24276)
sources.summary: IWM register entry for a brass plaque by the wall of the war memorial gardens at Westbury Gardens, Bradford-on-Avon. It commemorates the crew of Halifax LW693 'V', 425 Squadron RCAF, lost on 26 March 1944. The names on the plaque are not shown; the page text is a template with a '(NAMES)' placeholder. IWM states no maker, unveiling date or maintainer.

paragraphs.text: This memorial is for the crew of Halifax III LW693, code KW-V, of 425 (Alouette) Squadron RCAF, lost at Bradford on Avon, Wiltshire, on 26 March 1944. The aircraft flew from Tholthorpe on a training flight; the IBCC calls it a day cross-country exercise and War Memorials Online calls it a test flight leaving at 16:30. War Memorials Online gives the serial as LE693, where IWM and IBCC give LW693. It was not an operation over enemy territory.

War Memorials Online says the pilot lost control at about 10,000 ft over Wiltshire and ordered the crew to bail out. Witnesses saw the aircraft circling low over the town with an engine on fire. Men who jumped over the town were too low for their parachutes to open. The aircraft crashed in a field above the town and exploded; the pilot was killed, and townspeople pulled out the rear gunner, who died soon afterwards. A Canadian museum record puts the crash site in the Priory grounds at Christchurch. Six men died. The accounts of the survivors differ: IBCC names Cpl Craig Reid, a ground radar technician standing in for a colleague, and Sgt Bill Cameron, who it says was killed over Germany weeks later. War Memorials Online instead says the surviving mid-upper gunner died in Halifax LW672 over the Ruhr in July 1944. The Canadian record says two Canadians survived and gives no confirmed cause for the loss.

The dead were Pilot Officers Joseph Georges Brian Hall (pilot), Don Hernando Desoto Grover (navigator) and Roy Stanley Porter (bomb aimer), all RCAF, and Sergeants Harry Newton (wireless operator/air gunner, aged 22, of Oldham), Graham Herbert Evans (air gunner, aged 21, of Ystrad Mynach) and Frank Norman Simpson (flight engineer, aged 20, of Stretton).

The memorial is a brass plaque at Westbury House, St Margaret's Street, Bradford on Avon. IWM describes it as attached to a stone block by the wall of the war memorial gardens. War Memorials Online says it was unveiled in 1994 and that an ex-corporal radio technician flew in from Canada for it. The plaque has since been moved to a new position on the same site, and the page describes it as legible, with a wooden backing that will deteriorate outdoors. IWM does not show the names on the plaque, so no source here confirms that names are inscribed on it.

War Memorials Online lists Bradford on Avon Town Council as the custodian of the plaque. The council's own Westbury Garden page does not mention the plaque, and no source found shows an annual event there.

notes:
WHAT 24276 IS: a brass plaque at Westbury House / Westbury Gardens, Bradford on Avon, BA15 1DE, for the crew of Halifax III LW693 KW-V, 425 Sqn RCAF, lost 26 March 1944 on a training flight from Tholthorpe. It is a memorial to a training-flight crash, not an operation; it is Bomber Command (6 Group RCAF) aircrew. NOT Peak/Pennines: our stored summary of IWM 24276 ('Halifax crash site in Peak/Pennines region') is wrong and cannot be retracted by this tool (external_narratives); fix by hand. Coordinates: IWM 51.34668886515, -2.251819804889 (OS grid ST 82565 60870); WMO 51.346634, -2.251997. Our 52.2032, -1.7690 is Stratford-upon-Avon. Suggested title: 'Halifax LW693 (425 Sqn RCAF) Memorial Plaque, Bradford on Avon'. MERGE: the narrative, inscription and Bradford on Avon location/county, LW693 and crash_date are all correct and belong to IWM 24276; the Peak/Pennines summary, the Glossop contact (Derbyshire), the Stratford coordinates and the region_code PN-005 (Peak/Pennines) and what3words belong to something else or were guessed. The inscription's names line is the placeholder. DISCREPANCIES: serial LE693 (WMO) vs LW693 (IWM, IBCC, CASPIR); survivors and bail-out accounts differ between WMO, IBCC and CASPIR (recorded in text); crash site 'field above the town' (WMO) vs 'Priory grounds at Christchurch' (CASPIR). Hall and Porter are named only by CASPIR (IBCC gives initials 'Hall J G B', 'Porter R S'); I did not find their IBCC pages or CWGC pages, nor ages. CWGC links omitted (not read directly). IWM photos are credited to Jon Webber but I did not capture image URLs, so no photos included. Town council page and the plaque custodian rests on WMO alone.
